preamble: Palatalization of the voiceless velar stop [k] to the voiceless alveolo-palatal affricate [tɕ] before front vowels and [j]. In Mandarin, Middle Chinese velars before high front vowels and medial -j- merged with the alveolar sibilants into the alveolo-palatal series written j/q/x in Pinyin, so that 家 Middle Chinese kae is Mandarin jiā [tɕi̯ä], while Cantonese keeps [k] (gaa1). The same outcome arose independently in Southern Gyeongsang Korean, where ki is pronounced [tɕi], and in Finland Swedish, where historic k before front vowels is [tɕ] (kyrka /²tɕʏrka/ 'church'). In Romansh, Latin c before a became /tɕ/ (canem > Putèr chaun, Sursilvan tgaun 'dog').

examples.note: Dialectal palatalization of ki/ky to [tɕ] (Korean ㅈ); Seoul Korean keeps gireum [kiɾɯm].
Okinawan palatalized *k before *i; cf. Japanese kiri

examples.to: Putèr and Rumantsch Grischun chaun, Sursilvan tgaun, Vallader chan
Vallader and Rumantsch Grischun chasa, Putèr chesa 'house'
examples.note: ⟨ch⟩ and ⟨tg⟩ both spell /tɕ/. Sursilvan lacks the change in casa 'house'.
